newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products end higher on soybeans, exports.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products end higher on soybeans, exports.

text.p: CBOT soy product futures closed higher on gains in soybeans plus bullish input from the export sector, traders said.
"We had the reports to react to and they were generally supportive but not for corn," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.
USDA Thursday trimmed by 30 million bushels its estimate for 1996-97 U.S. soybean ending stocks and the government's weekly export sales report also was supportive.

USDA said for the week ended December 5 net export sales of soymeal totaled 147,200 tonnes. That was above expectations for 50,000 to 80,000 tonnes. Soyoil sales totaled 42,700 tonnes, above expectations for 10,000 to 15,000 tonnes. Traders also said there were rumors Thursday that China was buying U.S. soybeans and soymeal.
For the week ended December 5, China bought 54,500 tonnes of U.S. soymeal and 10,000 tonnes of soyoil, USDA said.
Griffin Trading bought 400 lots of January soymeal and Cargill Inc bought 800 lots of March soyoil, traders said.
Soymeal closed $2.90 to $4.10 per ton higher, with December up $4.10 at $235.70. Soyoil was 0.11 to 0.20 cent per lb higher, with December up 0.11 at 23.11 cents.
Soymeal futures volume was estimated at 23,000 contracts, below the 29,551 traded Wednesday, according to the CBOT.
Soyoil futures volume was estimated at 18,000 contracts, below the 21,131 traded Tuesday.
